findings.pdf_says: {1S EQUAL TO / IS =} (SEARCH Format 2, AND data-name-2 line; the first glyph of the upper choice is printed like the lowercase l / digit 1 of this typeface, while the identical choice on the WHEN data-name-1 line prints IS EQUAL TO)
findings.note: The markdown carries the misprint as the token '1S' with no editorial note, where the format means the optional word IS (as in the parallel WHEN data-name-1 line, 'IS EQUAL TO'). A grammar or reader taking the transcription literally sees a non-word in the format. Either transcribe it as IS with an editorial note recording the printed glyph, or keep it with a note. No effect on choice indicators, brackets, ellipses or underlining, which all match the print.
findings.why_it_matters: The SEARCH Format 2 AND line shows the non-word '1S' where the format means the optional word IS; a reader or grammar audit taking the transcription literally sees a token that is not a COBOL word.
